deai_text_1.result: Why AI Fails at Subnet Math: LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini regularly make errors on subnet boundaries. They confuse network and broadcast addresses, miscalculate the first and last usable host, drop the wildcard mask, and cannot reliably compute VLSM allocations. Network engineers and students cannot trust these results. Our tool uses exact integer arithmetic in your browser. Every broadcast address, every host range, every supernet boundary is computed bit-perfectly. No approximation, no hallucination, no guessing. You see the binary breakdown showing exactly which bits belong to the network and which belong to the host. Whether you are debugging a production VPN, sitting a CCNA exam, planning a small office network, or trying to figure out whether two CIDR blocks overlap, this tool gives answers you can deploy immediately.

deai_text_2.result: How to Use This Subnet Calculator: Type or paste any IPv4 or IPv6 address in CIDR notation, such as 192.168.1.0/24 or 2001:db8::/64. The tool instantly computes the network address, broadcast address, first and last host, total addresses, usable hosts, subnet mask in dotted decimal, wildcard mask for Cisco gear, and the IP class. For deeper work, switch to the VLSM tab to allocate variable-length subnets from a parent block based on host requirements. Use the Supernetting tab to summarize a list of networks into a single route. Use the Splitter tab to divide a network into N equal subnets. Use the Overlap tab to detect whether two networks conflict. Every calculation is local, every result is bit-exact, and nothing is sent to any server.

deai_text_3.result: Subnetting Frequently Asked Questions: What is a subnet mask and why does it matter? A subnet mask splits an IP address into a network portion and a host portion. Bits set to 1 identify the network, bits set to 0 identify hosts inside that network. The mask is what lets routers forward traffic to the right place. What is CIDR notation? CIDR stands for Classless Inter-Domain Routing. The slash number tells you how many leading bits are the network prefix. A /24 means 24 network bits and 8 host bits, which gives 256 total addresses and 254 usable hosts. Why is the first and last address reserved? The first address is the network identifier. The last address is the broadcast address used to send to every host in the subnet. What is VLSM? Variable Length Subnet Masking lets you carve a large network into smaller subnets of different sizes based on actual need, avoiding the waste of fixed-size subnets. What is a wildcard mask? It is the inverse of the subnet mask and is used in Cisco ACLs and OSPF network statements. Our tool computes both for you. Can this tool replace an exam study guide? Many CCNA and Network+ candidates use it as a quick reference while practicing. The binary breakdown makes the math visible.
